        private async Task DeleteNodeAsync(TreeViewNodeModel model)

        {

            switch (model.modelType)

            {

                case "rate":

                    await _tariffViewModel.DeleteRateTable((RateTableDto)model.returnData);

                    break;



                case "zone":

                    var parentRate = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == ((ZoneDTO)model.returnData).RateTableGuid);

                    parentRate?.RateTableZones.Remove((ZoneDTO)model.returnData);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parentRate);

                    break;



                case "rule":

                    var zone = _rateTables.SelectMany(rt => rt.RateTableZones)

                        .FirstOrDefault(z => z.Id == ((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData).ZoneGuid);

                    zone?.ZonePricingRule.Remove((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData);

                    var parent = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == zone?.RateTableGuid);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parent);

                    break;

            }



            await LoadAPIDataIntoMemory();

        }



        private async void DeleteNodeKeyPress(object sender, KeyEventArgs e)

        {

            if (e.KeyCode != Keys.Delete)

                return;



            var selectedNode = radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNode;

            if (selectedNode?.Tag is TreeViewNodeModel model)

            {

                try

                {

                    await DeleteNodeAsync(model);

                }

                catch (Exception ex)

                {

                    // Optional: Log or show error

                    MessageBox.Show($"Error deleting node: {ex.Message}", "Delete Error", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Error);

                }

            }

        }



        #region TreeViewStateHandler



        private void SaveExpandedStates(RadTreeNode nodeToSave)

        {

            {

                if (nodeToSave != null && nodeToSave.DataBoundItem != null)

                {

                    if (!nodeStates.ContainsKey(nodeToSave.DataBoundItem))

                    {

                        nodeStates.Add(nodeToSave.DataBoundItem, new State(nodeToSave.Expanded, nodeToSave.Selected));

                    }

                    else

                    {

                        nodeStates[nodeToSave.DataBoundItem] = new State(nodeToSave.Expanded, nodeToSave.Selected);

                    }

                }

                foreach (RadTreeNode childNode in nodeToSave.Nodes)

                {

                    SaveExpandedStates(childNode);

                }

            }

        }



        private void RestoreExpandedStates(RadTreeNode nodeToRestore)

        {

            if (nodeToRestore != null && nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem != null &&

                nodeStates.ContainsKey(nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem))

            {

                nodeToRestore.Expanded = nodeStates[nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem].Expanded;

                nodeToRestore.Selected = nodeStates[nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem].Selected;

            }



            foreach (RadTreeNode childNode in nodeToRestore.Nodes)

            {

                RestoreExpandedStates(childNode);

            }

        }

        public RadContextMenu GetTreeViewContextMenu(TreeViewNodeModel tag)

        {

            var contextMenu = new RadContextMenu();



            var deleteItem = new RadMenuItem("Delete") { Tag = tag };

            var renameItem = new RadMenuItem("Rename") { Tag = tag };



            deleteItem.Click += async (s, e) => await DeleteNodeAsync(tag);

            renameItem.Click += async (s, e) => SetNodeInEditMode(tag, this.Text, this);



            contextMenu.Items.AddRange(new RadItem[]

            {

                //new RadMenuItem("Export"),

                //new RadMenuItem("Export"),

                new RadMenuSeparatorItem(),

                renameItem,

                new RadMenuSeparatorItem(),

                deleteItem

            });



            return contextMenu;

        }

        private string GetHash(RateTableDto rateTable)

        {

            var options = new JsonSerializerOptions

            {

                DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull,

                PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase

            };



            var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(rateTable, options);



            using var sha = SHA256.Create();

            var bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(json);

            var hash = sha.ComputeHash(bytes);

            return System.Convert.ToBase64String(hash);

        }



        private void InitializeRateTableHashes(IEnumerable<RateTableDto> rateTables)

        {

            _rateTableHashes.Clear();

            foreach (var rateTable in rateTables)

            {

                _rateTableHashes[rateTable.Id] = GetHash(rateTable);

            }

        }

    internal struct State

    {

        public bool Expanded { get; set; }



        public bool Selected { get; set; }



        public State(bool expanded, bool selected) : this()

        {

            this.Expanded = expanded;

            this.Selected = selected;

        }

    }

## ASSISTANT
You're exactly right — you're calling the same `SaveToAPI` method across all bound events (including from tree events, form fields, grid edits, etc.), **but not updating the `RowVersion` across all references**. That leads to a mismatch on subsequent calls — and that’s where your **`404 RowVersion` error** is coming from.

---

### ✅ What’s happening?

When `SaveToAPI(rateTable)` succeeds:

```csharp
rateTable.RowVersion = updatedDto.RowVersion;
_currentRateTable = updatedDto;
```

That’s good, **but**:

- The grid’s bound list still references the *old object instances* (`WeightCostItemDto`, `ZoneDTO`, etc.) from before the update.
- Even if `RateTableDto`'s `RowVersion` is updated, the nested collections still hold stale objects.
- When one of those triggers a change again (like editing a cell in the weight grid), you're calling `SaveToAPI()` again...
- ...and it's serializing and submitting an object using the **previous `RowVersion`**, so you get a **404 on update** due to concurrency conflict.

---

### 🔧 Solution: Force RowVersion + Object Sync

Right after a successful update, **you should rebind your entire object tree** using the fresh `updatedDto`. You’re already assigning `_currentRateTable = updatedDto;`, which is a good start.

Now you just need to:

1. Replace your collections with the updated ones.
2. Re-bind the UI if needed.

---

### 🔁 Patch suggestion inside `SaveToAPI`

```csharp
private async Task SaveToAPI(RateTableDto rateTable)
{
    var currentHash = GetHash(rateTable);
    if (_rateTableHashes.TryGetValue(rateTable.Id, out var previousHash) && currentHash == previousHash)
        return;

    _pricingRuleBinding.EndEdit();
    _zoneBinding.EndEdit();
    _rateTableBinding.EndEdit();
    radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();
    radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();

    var result = await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(rateTable);

    if (result.Success && result.returnData is RateTableDto updatedDto)
    {
        // Update RowVersion & global reference
        _rateTableHashes[updatedDto.Id] = GetHash(updatedDto);
        _currentRateTable = updatedDto;

        // Re-assign UI binding source collections
        _currentZone = updatedDto.RateTableZones.FirstOrDefault(z => z.Id == _currentZone?.Id);
        _currentPricingRule = _currentZone?.ZonePricingRule.FirstOrDefault(r => r.Id == _currentPricingRule?.Id);

        if (_currentZone != null && _currentPricingRule != null)
        {
            DataBindForm(_currentRateTable, _currentZone, _currentPricingRule);
        }
    }
}
```

---

### 🧠 Optional Optimizations

- If `DataBindForm` is expensive, debounce it using `Task.Delay` or a dirty flag.
- Keep `_currentRateTable`, `_currentZone`, and `_currentPricingRule` always in sync with the last saved version.

---

## USER
radgrid how do i limit the input for decimal int

## ASSISTANT
To **limit input to `decimal` or `int` values** in a **Telerik `RadGridView`**, you can handle it cleanly using the **column’s `DataType`, `FormatString`, and `EditorRequired` or `CellEditorInitialized`** events.

---

### ✅ Option 1: Set `DataType` on the column

If you're adding columns manually:

```csharp
var col = new GridViewDecimalColumn("Cost");
col.FieldName = "cost";
col.HeaderText = "Cost";
col.DecimalPlaces = 2;               // Limit decimal precision
col.Minimum = 0;                     // Optional: set bounds
col.Maximum = 10000;
col.FormatString = "{0:F2}";        // Force two decimal places
col.DataType = typeof(decimal);     // ← THIS enforces decimal input
radGridView1.Columns.Add(col);
```

For integer:

```csharp
var col = new GridViewDecimalColumn("Weight");
col.FieldName = "weight";
col.HeaderText = "Weight";
col.DecimalPlaces = 0;
col.DataType = typeof(int);         // ← Forces int-only input
radGridView1.Columns.Add(col);
```

---

### ✅ Option 2: Enforce validation in `CellEditorInitialized`

If your column is auto-generated or you want more control:

```csharp
radGridView1.CellEditorInitialized += (s, e) =>
{
    if (e.Column.Name == "cost")
    {
        if (e.Editor is RadSpinEditor spinEditor)
        {
            spinEditor.Minimum = 0;
            spinEditor.Maximum = 10000;
            spinEditor.DecimalPlaces = 2;
            spinEditor.ThousandsSeparator = false;
        }
    }
};
```

For integers:

```csharp
if (e.Column.Name == "weight" && e.Editor is RadSpinEditor intEditor)
{
    intEditor.DecimalPlaces = 0;
    intEditor.Minimum = 0;
    intEditor.Maximum = 1000;
}
```

---

### ✅ Option 3: Validate via `CellValidating` (optional)

```csharp
radGridView1.CellValidating += (s, e) =>
{
    if (e.Column.Name == "cost")
    {
        if (!decimal.TryParse(e.Value?.ToString(), out var val))
        {
            e.Cancel = true;
            e.Row.ErrorText = "Please enter a valid decimal number.";
        }
    }
};
```

---

### ⚠️ Don’t forget
- For **auto-generated columns**, set `AutoGenerateColumns = false` and add them manually if you want full control.
- The `RadSpinEditor` is the default editor for `GridViewDecimalColumn` — it enforces types well.

---

## ASSISTANT
Yeah — sounds like the **three `RadGridView`s** (`radGridWeightCostRatio`, `radGridAccessorials`, `radGrid_ZipCodes`) are **data-bound**, and they display fine, but changes made *in the grid* aren’t triggering a save or aren't being pushed back into the bound object in a timely way.

Here’s the likely root of the issue and how to fix it:

---

### 🧠 Root Cause: Grid is bound to `BindingList<T>`, but changes don’t trigger `PropertyChanged`

You’re using:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.DataSource = new BindingList<WeightCostItemDto>(...)
```

That's correct — but for the grid to:
1. Reflect changes in the UI.
2. Detect changes to fire your update logic.

— the items in the list must implement `INotifyPropertyChanged` (✅ which they do) **and** be properly hooked for monitoring.

However, **RadGrid doesn’t automatically listen to internal changes** unless you hook into:

---

### ✅ Fix 1: Listen to `ValueChanged` or `CellValueChanged`

Wire up the `CellValueChanged` event:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.CellValueChanged += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};
```

Do the same for the others:

```csharp
radGridAccessorials.CellValueChanged += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};

radGrid_ZipCodes.CellValueChanged += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};
```

---

### ✅ Fix 2: End edits properly

Telerik grids don’t always commit the edit until the cell or row loses focus. You might also need:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.CellEndEdit += (s, e) =>
{
    radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit(); // Ensures data pushes back into object
};
```

You can also do this in `SaveToAPI`:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();
radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();
radGrid_ZipCodes.EndEdit();
```

(Which you are already doing, so you're halfway there.)

---

### ✅ Bonus: Use `BindingList<T>` with `INotifyPropertyChanged`

You're already doing this, and it's good. Just make sure your DTOs like `WeightCostItemDto`, `ZoneAccessorialDto`, etc. implement `INotifyPropertyChanged` correctly — which you’ve done.

---

### 🧪 Pro Tip for Debugging

Put breakpoints or logs in:

```csharp
public decimal Cost
{
    get => _cost;
    set
    {
        _cost = value;
        Log.Information("Cost changed to: " + value);
        OnPropertyChanged(nameof(Cost));
    }
}
```

If it doesn't hit — the UI isn't pushing changes back. If it *does* hit, but save doesn't — the `CellValueChanged` event might be missing.

## ASSISTANT
Thanks for posting the full DTO setup — and yes, these are wired beautifully with `INotifyPropertyChanged`, so you're in good shape there. The issue isn’t in the DTOs — it’s in how and **when** the Telerik RadGridView is committing edits *back to those DTOs*.

Let me break down what’s likely going wrong and how to make those three grids — especially `radGridWeightCostRatio` — actually trigger `SaveToAPI`.

---

## 🧩 Problem Summary

Even though your DTOs fire `PropertyChanged`, Telerik **does not push cell edits** into the bound object until:

- The user **exits the cell** _or_
- You explicitly call `.EndEdit()` on the grid or row.

This means you could **see changes visually**, but they aren’t written back to the object — and your `SaveToAPI()` won’t fire if the hash hasn’t changed.

---

## ✅ The Fix

### ✅ 1. Handle `CellEndEdit` or `CellValueChanged` for each grid

Right after `DataBindForm()`, add:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.CellEndEdit += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};

radGridAccessorials.CellEndEdit += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};

radGrid_ZipCodes.CellEndEdit += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};
```

> 🔁 Optional: You can use `.CellValueChanged` instead of `.CellEndEdit` — but `.CellEndEdit` tends to be more reliable in this context.

---

### ✅ 2. Optionally force commit before saving

If needed, in your `SaveToAPI`:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();
radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();
radGrid_ZipCodes.EndEdit();
```

You're already calling this — just make sure it's done **before checking the hash**.

---

### ✅ 3. BindingSource `.EndEdit()`

You’re doing this already:

```csharp
_pricingRuleBinding.EndEdit();
_zoneBinding.EndEdit();
_rateTableBinding.EndEdit();
```

That’s correct — **but it only works if the edits already pushed into the object**. Without `.EndEdit()` on the grid or row, it won’t flow.

---

### 🧪 Testing Tip

Try adding a temporary `Log.Information()` inside `WeightCostItemDto.cost` setter — if it doesn’t hit after cell edit, it means `.EndEdit()` hasn’t fired yet.

---

        {

            _tariffViewModel = tariffViewModel;

            SetScreenPosition();

            _ = InitializeAsync();

        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        private void SetScreenPosition()

        {

            var screen = Screen.FromControl(this).WorkingArea;

            this.Location = new Point((screen.Width - this.Width) / 2, 250); // center X, top Y

        }



        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        {

            WireEvents();

            ConfigureGui();

            await LoadAPIDataIntoMemory();  //fire the chain

            PopulateTreeView();

        }



        #region Start UP



        private void WireEvents()

        {

            //RadTreeview Actions

            radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNodeChanged += SelectedNodeChanged;

            radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNodeChanging += SelectedNodeChanging;

            radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.KeyDown += DeleteNodeKeyPress;

            appendZipCodesToolStripMenuItem.Click += AppendZipCodes_Click;

        }



       



        private void ConfigureGui()

        {

            HideServiceArea(true);

            HidePricingRules(true);

        }



        private async Task LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()

        {

            const int maxRetries = 10;

            const int delayMs = 10000;



            for (int i = 1; i <= maxRetries; i++)

            {

                try

                {

                    var result = await _tariffViewModel.GetRateTables();

                    if (result.Success)

                    {

                        try

                        {

                            if (result.Collection == null)

                            {

                                UpdateStatusStripMessage("Connection Established - Data did not emerge.");

                                SendDektopAlert("API Connection was successful. ERROR: Data not retrieved", "ERROR");

                                return;

                            }



                            _rateTables = result.Collection;

                            InitializeRateTableHashes(_rateTables);



                            foreach (var rateTable in _rateTables)

                            {

                                // Watch top-level rate table changes

                                rateTable.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                // Hook into zone collection changes

                                rateTable.RateTableZones.CollectionChanged += async (s, e) =>

                                {

                                    if (e.NewItems != null)

                                    {

                                        foreach (ZoneDTO zone in e.NewItems)

                                        {

                                            zone.PropertyChanged += async (zs, ze) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                            foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)

                                            {

                                                rule.PropertyChanged += async (rs, re) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                            }

                                        }

                                    }



                                    if (e.OldItems != null)

                                    {

                                        foreach (ZoneDTO zone in e.OldItems)

                                        {

                                            zone.PropertyChanged -= async (zs, ze) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                            foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)

                                            {

                                                rule.PropertyChanged -= async (rs, re) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                            }

                                        }

                                    }



                                    await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                };



                                // Hook into existing zones and rules

                                foreach (var zone in rateTable.RateTableZones)

                                {

                                    zone.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                    foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)

                                    {

                                        rule.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                    }

                                }

                            }

                        }

                        catch (Exception ex)

                        {

                            UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Connection Failed: {ex.Message}");

                            SendDektopAlert("API Connection failed", "ERROR");

                        }



                        return; // Success, exit early

                    }



                    UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Attempting to connect to API - Try #{i} ({result.Message ?? "No error detail"})");

                }

                catch (Exception ex)

                {

                    UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Attempt #{i} failed: {ex.Message}");

                }



                await Task.Delay(delayMs); // wait before retrying

            }



            UpdateStatusStripMessage("❌ Failed to connect to API after multiple attempts. Service may be unavailable.");

            SendDektopAlert("Failed to connect to API after multiple attempts. Service may be unavailable.", "ERROR - API Connection Failure");

        }



        #endregion Start UP

        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        private void PopulateTreeView()

        {

            radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNodeChanged -= SelectedNodeChanged;



            this.radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.DataSource = _rateTables;

            this.radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.DisplayMember = "TarriffTableName\\ZoneName\\RuleName";

            this.radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.ChildMember = "RateTableZones\\RateTableZones\\ZonePricingRule";

            radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNodeChanged += SelectedNodeChanged;

        }

        private void SelectedNodeChanging(object sender, RadTreeViewCancelEventArgs e)

        {



        }

        private void SelectedNodeChanged(object sender, RadTreeViewEventArgs e)

        {

            if (e.Node?.DataBoundItem == null) return;



            var data = e.Node.DataBoundItem;



            switch (data)

            {

                case RateTableDto rate:

                    _currentPricingRule = null;

                    _currentZone = null;



                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != rate.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = rate;

                    }



                    btnAddRule.Enabled = false;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = true;

                    HideServiceArea(true);

                    HidePricingRules(true);

                    headerLabel.Text = _currentRateTable.TarriffTableName;

                    break;



                case ZoneDTO zone:

                    if (_currentZone == null || _currentZone.Id != zone.Id)

                    {

                        _currentZone = zone;

                    }



                    var parentRate = e.Node.Parent?.DataBoundItem as RateTableDto;

                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != parentRate?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = parentRate;

                    }



                    _currentPricingRule = null;



                    btnAddRule.Enabled = true;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = true;

                    HideServiceArea(false);

                    HidePricingRules(true);

                    headerLabel.Text = $"{_currentRateTable?.TarriffTableName} - {_currentZone.ZoneName}";

                    break;



                case PricingRuleDto rule:

                    if (_currentPricingRule == null || _currentPricingRule.Id != rule.Id)

                    {

                        _currentPricingRule = rule;

                    }



                    var newZone = e.Node.Parent?.DataBoundItem as ZoneDTO;

                    if (_currentZone == null || _currentZone.Id != newZone?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentZone = newZone;

                    }



                    var newRateTable = e.Node.Parent?.Parent?.DataBoundItem as RateTableDto;

                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != newRateTable?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = newRateTable;

                    }



                    DataBindForm(_currentRateTable, _currentZone, _currentPricingRule);



                    headerLabel.Text = $"{_currentRateTable?.TarriffTableName} - {_currentZone?.ZoneName} - {_currentPricingRule?.RuleName}";

                    btnAddRule.Enabled = true;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = false;

                    HidePricingRules(false);

                    HideServiceArea(false);

                    break;

            }

        }





        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        /// <param name="rateTable"></param>

        /// <returns></returns>

        private async Task SaveToAPI(RateTableDto rateTable)

        {

            var currentHash = GetHash(rateTable);

            if (_rateTableHashes.TryGetValue(rateTable.Id, out var previousHash) && currentHash == previousHash)

                return;



            _pricingRuleBinding.EndEdit();

            _zoneBinding.EndEdit();

            _rateTableBinding.EndEdit();

            radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();

            radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();



            var result = await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(rateTable);



            if (result.Success && result.returnData is RateTableDto updatedDto)

            {

                rateTable.RowVersion = updatedDto.RowVersion;

                _currentRateTable = updatedDto;

                _rateTableHashes[rateTable.Id] = GetHash(updatedDto); // Update snapshot

            }



            return;

        }

        private async Task DeleteNodeAsync(TreeViewNodeModel model)

        {

            switch (model.modelType)

            {

                case "rate":

                    await _tariffViewModel.DeleteRateTable((RateTableDto)model.returnData);

                    break;



                case "zone":

                    var parentRate = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == ((ZoneDTO)model.returnData).RateTableGuid);

                    parentRate?.RateTableZones.Remove((ZoneDTO)model.returnData);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parentRate);

                    break;



                case "rule":

                    var zone = _rateTables.SelectMany(rt => rt.RateTableZones)

                        .FirstOrDefault(z => z.Id == ((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData).ZoneGuid);

                    zone?.ZonePricingRule.Remove((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData);

                    var parent = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == zone?.RateTableGuid);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parent);

                    break;

            }



            await LoadAPIDataIntoMemory();

        }

                try

                catch (Exception ex)

                    MessageBox.Show($"Error deleting node: {ex.Message}", "Delete Error", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Error);

                }

            }

        }

        private void SaveExpandedStates(RadTreeNode nodeToSave)

        {

            {

                if (nodeToSave != null && nodeToSave.DataBoundItem != null)

                {

                    if (!nodeStates.ContainsKey(nodeToSave.DataBoundItem))

                    {

                        nodeStates.Add(nodeToSave.DataBoundItem, new State(nodeToSave.Expanded, nodeToSave.Selected));

                    }

                    else

                    {

                        nodeStates[nodeToSave.DataBoundItem] = new State(nodeToSave.Expanded, nodeToSave.Selected);

                    }

                }

                foreach (RadTreeNode childNode in nodeToSave.Nodes)

                {

                    SaveExpandedStates(childNode);

                }

            }

        private void RestoreExpandedStates(RadTreeNode nodeToRestore)

        {

            if (nodeToRestore != null && nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem != null &&

                nodeStates.ContainsKey(nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem))

            {

                nodeToRestore.Expanded = nodeStates[nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem].Expanded;

                nodeToRestore.Selected = nodeStates[nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem].Selected;

            }



            foreach (RadTreeNode childNode in nodeToRestore.Nodes)

            {

                RestoreExpandedStates(childNode);

            }

        }

        private string GetHash(RateTableDto rateTable)

        {

            var options = new JsonSerializerOptions

            {

                DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull,

                PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase

            };



            var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(rateTable, options);



            using var sha = SHA256.Create();

            var bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(json);

            var hash = sha.ComputeHash(bytes);

            return System.Convert.ToBase64String(hash);

        }



        private void InitializeRateTableHashes(IEnumerable<RateTableDto> rateTables)

        {

            _rateTableHashes.Clear();

            foreach (var rateTable in rateTables)

            {

                _rateTableHashes[rateTable.Id] = GetHash(rateTable);

            }

        }

    }



    internal struct State

    {

        public bool Expanded { get; set; }



        public bool Selected { get; set; }



        public State(bool expanded, bool selected) : this()

        {

            this.Expanded = expanded;

            this.Selected = selected;

        }

    }

You're very close, and you’ve already nailed a big chunk of it. But you're right — something **is missing**. And it comes down to how Telerik RadGridView handles **edit lifecycle events** and **bound object updates**.

---

## 🔍 What’s likely missing

Right now you are using:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.CellEndEdit += async (s, e) =>
```

Which works **sometimes**, but **not always**. Here's why:

1. **CellEndEdit only fires** after a cell is committed — but this doesn’t always happen (e.g. moving directly to another control can skip it).
2. **Data isn’t pushed into the object** if edit isn’t committed (i.e., if focus changes rapidly).

---

## ✅ Recommended fix: handle `RowValidated`

The safest and most consistent event to use for saving is:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.RowValidated += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};
```

Repeat that for the other two grids:

```csharp
radGridAccessorials.RowValidated += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};

radGrid_ZipCodes.RowValidated += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};
```

> ✅ `RowValidated` is more reliable than `CellEndEdit`, especially when you have async/await operations in play.

---

## 🧼 Bonus: Ensure edits are committed before save

If needed, right before `SaveToAPI`, do:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();
radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();
radGrid_ZipCodes.EndEdit();
```

But again — **`RowValidated` should cover the actual object update**, so `EndEdit()` becomes a nice-to-have.

---

## ✅ TL;DR Integration Plan

In your `DataBindForm()` method, **replace** the `CellEndEdit` handlers with:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.RowValidated += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};

radGridAccessorials.RowValidated += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};

radGrid_ZipCodes.RowValidated += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (_currentRateTable != null)
        await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
};
```

And you should see **clean, consistent, and correct** update behavior.

Let me know if you'd like these encapsulated into a shared `BindGridSaveHandler()` method or any other niceties.

​To limit decimal input in a Telerik RadGridView for WinForms, you can utilize the `GridViewDecimalColumn` and configure its properties to enforce the desired constraints. Here's how you can achieve this:

### 1. Configure the Decimal Column

Create a `GridViewDecimalColumn` and set its properties to define the number of decimal places and the display format:

```csharp
GridViewDecimalColumn decimalColumn = new GridViewDecimalColumn();
decimalColumn.Name = "DecimalColumn";
decimalColumn.HeaderText = "Unit Price";
decimalColumn.FieldName = "UnitPrice";
decimalColumn.DecimalPlaces = 2; // Limits input to 2 decimal places
decimalColumn.FormatString = "{0:N2}"; // Formats display to 2 decimal places
radGridView1.MasterTemplate.Columns.Add(decimalColumn);
```


This configuration ensures that users can input values with up to two decimal places, and the values are displayed accordingly. citeturn0search0

### 2. Implement Validation for Decimal Input

To enforce additional validation rules, such as restricting the range of acceptable values, handle the `CellValidating` event:

```csharp
private void radGridView1_CellValidating(object sender, CellValidatingEventArgs e)
{
    if (e.Column.Name == "DecimalColumn")
    {
        if (decimal.TryParse(e.Value?.ToString(), out decimal newValue))
        {
            if (newValue < 0 || newValue > 1000)
            {
                e.Cancel = true;
                ((GridViewDataRowInfo)e.Row).ErrorText = "Value must be between 0 and 1000.";
            }
            else
            {
                ((GridViewDataRowInfo)e.Row).ErrorText = string.Empty;
            }
        }
        else
        {
            e.Cancel = true;
            ((GridViewDataRowInfo)e.Row).ErrorText = "Invalid decimal value.";
        }
    }
}
```


This event handler validates the input, ensuring it falls within the specified range, and provides user feedback when the input is invalid. citeturn0search5

### 3. Customize the Spin Editor (Optional)

If you require more control over the input behavior, such as disabling the up/down buttons in the spin editor, you can handle the `CellEditorInitialized` event:

```csharp
private void radGridView1_CellEditorInitialized(object sender, GridViewCellEventArgs e)
{
    if (e.Column.Name == "DecimalColumn")
    {
        GridSpinEditor spinEditor = this.radGridView1.ActiveEditor as GridSpinEditor;
        if (spinEditor != null)
        {
            ((RadSpinEditorElement)spinEditor.EditorElement).ShowUpDownButtons = false;
        }
    }
}
```


This customization enhances the user experience by tailoring the editor to your application's specific needs. citeturn0search0

By implementing these configurations and event handlers, you can effectively limit and validate decimal input within your RadGridView.

## ASSISTANT
​To ensure that changes in your Telerik RadGridView are properly captured and saved, especially when dealing with decimal and integer inputs, it's crucial to handle data binding and related events correctly. Here's how you can achieve this:

---

### 🔄 Handling Data Binding and Change Events in RadGridView

1. **Use `CellValueChanged` and `RowValidated` Events**: These events are essential for detecting changes in cell values and validating rows after edits. Implementing these will help in capturing user inputs effectively.

   **Example**:
   ```csharp
   radGridView1.CellValueChanged += (s, e) =>
   {
       // Handle cell value change
       SaveChanges();
   };

   radGridView1.RowValidated += (s, e) =>
   {
       // Handle row validation
       SaveChanges();
   };
   ```


   These events ensure that any modifications made by the user are detected and can be processed accordingly.

2. **Implement `INotifyPropertyChanged` in Your Data Models**: Ensure that your data models, such as `WeightCostItemDto`, implement the `INotifyPropertyChanged` interface. This allows the UI to respond to property changes in the underlying data source.

   **Example**:
   ```csharp
   public class WeightCostItemDto : INotifyPropertyChanged
   {
       private decimal _cost;
       public decimal Cost
       {
           get => _cost;
           set
           {
               if (_cost != value)
               {
                   _cost = value;
                   OnPropertyChanged(nameof(Cost));
               }
           }
       }

       public event PropertyChangedEventHandler PropertyChanged;
       protected void OnPropertyChanged(string propertyName)
       {
           PropertyChanged?.Invoke(this, new PropertyChangedEventArgs(propertyName));
       }
   }
   ```


   This implementation ensures that changes to properties like `Cost` are propagated to the UI.

3. **Bind to a `BindingList<T>`**: When setting the `DataSource` of your RadGridView, use a `BindingList<T>` instead of a `List<T>`. `BindingList<T>` provides change notifications, which are essential for the grid to respond to data modifications.

   **Example**:
   ```csharp
   var bindingList = new BindingList<WeightCostItemDto>(yourDataList);
   radGridView1.DataSource = bindingList;
   ```


   This approach ensures that the grid is aware of any changes in the data source.

4. **Limit Decimal and Integer Inputs**: To restrict user input to valid decimal or integer values, configure the column editors appropriately.

   **Example for Decimal Input**:
   ```csharp
   GridViewDecimalColumn decimalColumn = new GridViewDecimalColumn("Cost");
   decimalColumn.DecimalPlaces = 2;
   decimalColumn.Minimum = 0;
   decimalColumn.Maximum = 1000;
   radGridView1.Columns.Add(decimalColumn);
   ```


   This setup ensures that users can only input decimal values within the specified range and precision.

---

By implementing these strategies, you can ensure that your RadGridView captures and processes user inputs effectively, maintaining data integrity and providing a responsive user experience.

If you need further assistance or have specific scenarios you'd like to address, feel free to ask!

This code is a simple example demonstrating how to use a **`BindingList<T>`** with **Telerik's RadGridView** in **WinForms** to track and react to changes in a data-bound list.

---

### 🔍 What It Does:

1. **Creates a `BindingList<MyObject>`**:
   ```csharp
   myList = new BindingList<MyObject>();
   ```
   `BindingList<T>` provides change notifications which are essential for automatic UI updates **and** for triggering `ListChanged` events when the list changes (add/remove/update).

2. **Populates the list** with `MyObject` instances (each having something like an ID and a string description).

3. **Attaches an event handler** to the list:
   ```csharp
   myList.ListChanged += new ListChangedEventHandler(myList_ListChanged);
   ```
   This lets you **track changes** (e.g., adding, removing, editing an item) at the **collection level**.

4. **Binds the list to a RadGridView**:
   ```csharp
   radGridView1.DataSource = myList;
   ```
   Any changes to `myList` are **reflected automatically in the grid**.

5. **Handles the `ListChanged` event**:
   ```csharp
   void myList_ListChanged(object sender, ListChangedEventArgs e)
   {
       MessageBox.Show(e.ListChangedType.ToString() + ": at index: " + e.NewIndex.ToString() + ", \"" + myList[e.NewIndex].MyString + "\"");
   }
   ```
   This displays a message box every time the list changes—showing what type of change occurred and what item was involved.

6. **Adds a new item on button click**:
   ```csharp
   myList.Add(new MyObject(6, "Plants"));
   ```
   This simulates user-driven list updates from outside the grid.

---

### ✅ Why This Matters:

If you're using Telerik’s `RadGridView` (like in your project), **this is the correct approach** when you want:

- Reactive UI (grid auto-updates)
- Notifications when the list changes
- Clean, decoupled data management

---

### 🧠 Final Tips for Your Case:

- Use `BindingList<T>` **everywhere** you're binding to the grid.
- Always ensure your objects implement `INotifyPropertyChanged` to handle **item-level changes**.
- Hook into `ListChanged` for **collection-level actions** (e.g., adding/removing).

## ASSISTANT
Great question. Let's cut straight to the core:

---

### ✅ Do you **need** `BindingList<T>`?

Yes, **if** you want the following from your **Telerik RadGridView**:

| Feature                                  | Requires `BindingList<T>` |
|------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| Auto UI updates when adding/removing     | ✅ Yes                     |
| `ListChanged` events for row saves       | ✅ Yes                     |
| Editable rows in grid                    | ✅ Yes                     |
| Detecting row-level add/remove/change    | ✅ Yes                     |
| Deep data binding (e.g. nested objects)  | ✅ Yes (plus `INotifyPropertyChanged`) |

If you're using a plain `List<T>`, **the grid won’t know** when something is added, removed, or changed. It’ll display the data—but it’s “dead” to events.

---

### 🔥 In Your Case

You're already doing the right thing with:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.DataSource = new BindingList<WeightCostItemDto>(ruleDto.WeightCostCollection);
```

But here's the **catch**:

Even with `BindingList<T>`, **edits to individual properties in the list's items won't trigger `ListChanged` unless**:

1. The objects (`WeightCostItemDto`, `ZoneAccessorialDto`, etc.) implement `INotifyPropertyChanged` – ✅ You're doing this!
2. The UI grid triggers `EndEdit` (handled automatically if user leaves the cell correctly, but you may need `CellEndEdit` to force it).
3. You don't suppress notifications (e.g., turning off `RaiseListChangedEvents = false`).

---

### 🧩 So do you need to hook `ListChanged`?

Only **if** you want to catch *add/remove* actions **outside the grid** or track all changes *manually*. Otherwise, you can rely on the `CellEndEdit` you already added:

```csharp
radGridWeightCostRatio.CellEndEdit += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(_currentRateTable);
```

This is **more precise** for save-on-edit logic.

---

### ✅ Summary

| You want this behavior                       | Use `BindingList<T>`? | Need `ListChanged`? |
|---------------------------------------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| Grid reflects new items immediately          | ✅ Yes                 | ❌ Optional         |
| Grid detects row edit and fires save         | ✅ Yes                 | ❌ CellEndEdit better |
| Manual add/remove from code updates grid     | ✅ Yes                 | ✅ Yes              |
| Deep nested binding with updates             | ✅ Yes                 | ❌ Only if needed   |

So bottom line:  
**Yes, keep using `BindingList<T>`**,  
**Only use `ListChanged` if you need event-driven behavior beyond the grid itself.**

        private async Task LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()

        {

            const int maxRetries = 10;

            const int delayMs = 10000;



            for (int i = 1; i <= maxRetries; i++)

            {

                try

                {

                    var result = await _tariffViewModel.GetRateTables();

                    if (result.Success)

                    {

                        try

                        {

                            if (result.Collection == null)

                            {

                                UpdateStatusStripMessage("Connection Established - Data did not emerge.");

                                SendDektopAlert("API Connection was successful. ERROR: Data not retrieved", "ERROR");

                                return;

                            }



                            _rateTables = result.Collection;

                            InitializeRateTableHashes(_rateTables);



                            foreach (var rateTable in _rateTables)

                            {

                                // Watch top-level rate table changes

                                rateTable.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                // Hook into zone collection changes

                                rateTable.RateTableZones.CollectionChanged += async (s, e) =>

                                {

                                    if (e.NewItems != null)

                                    {

                                        foreach (ZoneDTO zone in e.NewItems)

                                        {

                                            zone.PropertyChanged += async (zs, ze) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                            foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)

                                            {

                                                rule.PropertyChanged += async (rs, re) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                            }

                                        }

                                    }



                                    if (e.OldItems != null)

                                    {

                                        foreach (ZoneDTO zone in e.OldItems)

                                        {

                                            zone.PropertyChanged -= async (zs, ze) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                            foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)

                                            {

                                                rule.PropertyChanged -= async (rs, re) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                            }

                                        }

                                    }



                                    await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                };



                                // Hook into existing zones and rules

                                foreach (var zone in rateTable.RateTableZones)

                                {

                                    zone.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);



                                    foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)

                                    {

                                        rule.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);

                                    }

                                }

                            }

                        }

                        catch (Exception ex)

                        {

                            UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Connection Failed: {ex.Message}");

                            SendDektopAlert("API Connection failed", "ERROR");

                        }



                        return; // Success, exit early

                    }



                    UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Attempting to connect to API - Try #{i} ({result.Message ?? "No error detail"})");

                }

                catch (Exception ex)

                {

                    UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Attempt #{i} failed: {ex.Message}");

                }



                await Task.Delay(delayMs); // wait before retrying

            }



            UpdateStatusStripMessage("❌ Failed to connect to API after multiple attempts. Service may be unavailable.");

            SendDektopAlert("Failed to connect to API after multiple attempts. Service may be unavailable.", "ERROR - API Connection Failure");

        }

        private void SelectedNodeChanged(object sender, RadTreeViewEventArgs e)

        {

            if (e.Node?.DataBoundItem == null) return;



            var data = e.Node.DataBoundItem;



            switch (data)

            {

                case RateTableDto rate:

                    _currentPricingRule = null;

                    _currentZone = null;



                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != rate.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = rate;

                    }



                    btnAddRule.Enabled = false;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = true;

                    HideServiceArea(true);

                    HidePricingRules(true);

                    headerLabel.Text = _currentRateTable.TarriffTableName;

                    break;



                case ZoneDTO zone:

                    if (_currentZone == null || _currentZone.Id != zone.Id)

                    {

                        _currentZone = zone;

                    }



                    var parentRate = e.Node.Parent?.DataBoundItem as RateTableDto;

                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != parentRate?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = parentRate;

                    }



                    _currentPricingRule = null;



                    btnAddRule.Enabled = true;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = true;

                    HideServiceArea(false);

                    HidePricingRules(true);

                    headerLabel.Text = $"{_currentRateTable?.TarriffTableName} - {_currentZone.ZoneName}";

                    break;



                case PricingRuleDto rule:

                    if (_currentPricingRule == null || _currentPricingRule.Id != rule.Id)

                    {

                        _currentPricingRule = rule;

                    }



                    var newZone = e.Node.Parent?.DataBoundItem as ZoneDTO;

                    if (_currentZone == null || _currentZone.Id != newZone?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentZone = newZone;

                    }



                    var newRateTable = e.Node.Parent?.Parent?.DataBoundItem as RateTableDto;

                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != newRateTable?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = newRateTable;

                    }



                    DataBindForm(_currentRateTable, _currentZone, _currentPricingRule);



                    headerLabel.Text = $"{_currentRateTable?.TarriffTableName} - {_currentZone?.ZoneName} - {_currentPricingRule?.RuleName}";

                    btnAddRule.Enabled = true;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = false;

                    HidePricingRules(false);

                    HideServiceArea(false);

                    break;

            }

        }





        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        /// <param name="rateTable"></param>

        /// <returns></returns>

        private async Task SaveToAPI(RateTableDto rateTable)

        {

            var currentHash = GetHash(rateTable);

            if (_rateTableHashes.TryGetValue(rateTable.Id, out var previousHash) && currentHash == previousHash)

                return;



            _pricingRuleBinding.EndEdit();

            _zoneBinding.EndEdit();

            _rateTableBinding.EndEdit();

            radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();

            radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();



            var result = await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(rateTable);



            if (result.Success && result.returnData is RateTableDto updatedDto)

            {

                rateTable.RowVersion = updatedDto.RowVersion;

                _currentRateTable = updatedDto;

                _rateTableHashes[rateTable.Id] = GetHash(updatedDto); // Update snapshot

            }



            return;

        }

        private void SetNodeInEditMode(TreeViewNodeModel model, string newName, object sender)

        {

            RadTreeNode node = radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNode;

                node.BeginEdit(); // Optional: if you want inline editing

            }

        private async Task DeleteNodeAsync(TreeViewNodeModel model)

        {

            switch (model.modelType)

            {

                case "rate":

                    await _tariffViewModel.DeleteRateTable((RateTableDto)model.returnData);

                    break;



                case "zone":

                    var parentRate = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == ((ZoneDTO)model.returnData).RateTableGuid);

                    parentRate?.RateTableZones.Remove((ZoneDTO)model.returnData);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parentRate);

                    break;



                case "rule":

                    var zone = _rateTables.SelectMany(rt => rt.RateTableZones)

                        .FirstOrDefault(z => z.Id == ((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData).ZoneGuid);

                    zone?.ZonePricingRule.Remove((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData);

                    var parent = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == zone?.RateTableGuid);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parent);

                    break;

            }



            await LoadAPIDataIntoMemory();

        }



        private async void DeleteNodeKeyPress(object sender, KeyEventArgs e)

        {

            if (e.KeyCode != Keys.Delete)

                return;



            var selectedNode = radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNode;

            if (selectedNode?.Tag is TreeViewNodeModel model)

            {

                try

                {

                    await DeleteNodeAsync(model);

                }

                catch (Exception ex)

                {

                    // Optional: Log or show error

                    MessageBox.Show($"Error deleting node: {ex.Message}", "Delete Error", MessageBoxButtons.OK, MessageBoxIcon.Error);

                }

            }

        }



        #region TreeViewStateHandler



        private void SaveExpandedStates(RadTreeNode nodeToSave)

        {

            {

                if (nodeToSave != null && nodeToSave.DataBoundItem != null)

                {

                    if (!nodeStates.ContainsKey(nodeToSave.DataBoundItem))

                    {

                        nodeStates.Add(nodeToSave.DataBoundItem, new State(nodeToSave.Expanded, nodeToSave.Selected));

                    }

                    else

                    {

                        nodeStates[nodeToSave.DataBoundItem] = new State(nodeToSave.Expanded, nodeToSave.Selected);

                    }

                }

                foreach (RadTreeNode childNode in nodeToSave.Nodes)

                {

                    SaveExpandedStates(childNode);

                }

            }

        }



        private void RestoreExpandedStates(RadTreeNode nodeToRestore)

        {

            if (nodeToRestore != null && nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem != null &&

                nodeStates.ContainsKey(nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem))

            {

                nodeToRestore.Expanded = nodeStates[nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem].Expanded;

                nodeToRestore.Selected = nodeStates[nodeToRestore.DataBoundItem].Selected;

            }



            foreach (RadTreeNode childNode in nodeToRestore.Nodes)

            {

                RestoreExpandedStates(childNode);

            }

        }



        #endregion TreeViewStateHandler

            {

                //new RadMenuItem("Export"),

                //new RadMenuItem("Export"),

                new RadMenuSeparatorItem(),

                renameItem,

                new RadMenuSeparatorItem(),

                deleteItem

            });



            return contextMenu;

        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        /// <param name="storedDays"></param>

        private void PopulateCheckedDaysFromDto(string storedDays)

        {

            var selected = (storedDays ?? "").Split(',', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries);

            foreach (var item in selected.Distinct())

            {

                var match = inputDayOfTheWeek.ListViewElement.Items.FirstOrDefault(e => (string)e.Text == item);

## ASSISTANT
**Yes**, you're exactly right. That’s a critical insight.

The **`EndEdit()`** call commits the changes from the UI-bound controls back into the underlying object model. Without it:

- The user's edits are still in the UI control's buffer.
- Your `GetHash(rateTable)` call is hashing **stale data**.
- So when the actual `UpdateRateTable(rateTable)` call fires, it saves the new data...
- But your hash table is still holding the pre-edit hash.
- Result: the next time a `PropertyChanged` or `ListChanged` event fires, **it sees a change**, and fires **again**.

### ✅ Fix Summary

Make sure **`EndEdit()` is called BEFORE** the hash check:

```csharp
private async Task SaveToAPI(RateTableDto rateTable)
{
    _pricingRuleBinding.EndEdit();
    _zoneBinding.EndEdit();
    _rateTableBinding.EndEdit();
    radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();
    radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();

    var currentHash = GetHash(rateTable);
    if (_rateTableHashes.TryGetValue(rateTable.Id, out var previousHash) && currentHash == previousHash)
        return;

    var result = await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(rateTable);

    if (result.Success && result.returnData is RateTableDto updatedDto)
    {
        rateTable.RowVersion = updatedDto.RowVersion;
        _currentRateTable = updatedDto;
        _rateTableHashes[rateTable.Id] = GetHash(updatedDto); // update snapshot
    }
}
```

### 🔄 Why This Works

Now the hash is always taken **after all UI edits are flushed into the DTO**, ensuring the comparison reflects reality.

### 🔍 Problem: JSON Serialization Doesn’t Pick Up Changes

But **that method doesn’t traverse deep binding sources or private setters well**, and **it doesn’t always catch changes** in `BindingList<T>` or complex child objects unless they’re public and fully hydrated.

### ✅ Solution: Use `JsonSerializerOptions.IncludeFields` and flatten properly

You can try this as a **quick fix**:

```csharp
{

    WriteIndented = false
};
```

But even **that might not be enough**.

### ✅ Better Fix: Serialize just the parts you care about for hashing

Instead of hashing the whole object (which may be big and inconsistent), hash a custom flattened structure like:

```csharp
private string GetRateTableHash(RateTableDto dto)
{
    var flattened = new
    {
        dto.Id,
        dto.TarriffTableName,
        Zones = dto.RateTableZones.Select(z => new
        {
            z.Id,
            z.ZoneName,
            Rules = z.ZonePricingRule.Select(r => new
            {
                r.Id,
                r.RuleName,
                r.ValidStartDate,
                r.ValidEndDate,
                r.OnDays,
                r.ValidHoursStart,
                r.ValidHoursEnd,
                r.RequiresQuote,
                r.MarkupType,
                r.MarkupCost,
                r.MaxCost,
                r.MinCost,
                Weights = r.WeightCostCollection.Select(w => new { w.weight, w.cost }).ToList()
            }).ToList()
        }).ToList()
    };

    var json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(flattened, new JsonSerializerOptions
    {
        PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
        WriteIndented = false
    });

    using var sha = SHA256.Create();
    var bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(json);
    var hash = sha.ComputeHash(bytes);
    return Convert.ToBase64String(hash);
}
```

Then call:

```csharp

```

---

### 💡 Why this works

You’re **not relying on JSON to magically catch all nested changes** anymore. You’re explicitly flattening and serializing **only the parts that matter**, guaranteeing consistent and complete hashing.

## ASSISTANT
Yeah, totally — **a recursive approach will work better** than relying on `JsonSerializer.Serialize(rateTable)` directly, especially if you have nested lists and property-changed tracking all over.

Right now your serializer probably **misses nested dirty changes** unless those objects were re-referenced (which isn't the case with bound grids).

---

### ✅ Here's a drop-in recursive hash generator

We’ll walk the object recursively, serialize only public data, and generate a clean hash string:

```csharp
private string GetHash(object obj)
{
    var sb = new StringBuilder();
    var visited = new HashSet<object>();

    void Walk(object target)
    {
        if (target == null || visited.Contains(target))
            return;

        visited.Add(target);

        var type = target.GetType();

        if (type.IsPrimitive || target is string || target is decimal || target is DateTime || target is Guid)
        {
            sb.Append(target.ToString());
            return;
        }

        if (target is IEnumerable<object> list)
        {
            foreach (var item in list)
                Walk(item);
            return;
        }

        foreach (var prop in type.GetProperties(System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Public | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance))
        {
            if (prop.GetIndexParameters().Length > 0)
                continue;

            var value = prop.GetValue(target);
            if (value is IEnumerable<object> subList)
            {
                foreach (var sub in subList)
                    Walk(sub);
            }
            else
            {
                Walk(value);
            }
        }
    }

    Walk(obj);

    using var sha = SHA256.Create();
    var bytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(sb.ToString());
    var hash = sha.ComputeHash(bytes);
    return Convert.ToBase64String(hash);
}
```

---

### ✅ How to use it

Just replace your `GetHash(RateTableDto rateTable)` with:

```csharp
private string GetHash(RateTableDto rateTable)
{
    return GetHash((object)rateTable);
}
```

---

### ✅ Why this works

This recursive walker:
- Handles deep nested objects/lists
- Ignores nulls and circular references
- Doesn't depend on JSON quirks
- Guarantees a stable string for hashing

Here’s a simplified and more effective version that captures the **entire tree structure state** — including **selected node identity** — and re-selects the same node after a reload.

### ✅ New Version – Save & Restore TreeView State

```csharp
private object _previouslySelectedItem;

private void SaveTreeState()
{
    if (radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNode?.DataBoundItem is object selectedItem)
    {
        _previouslySelectedItem = selectedItem;
    }
}

private void RestoreTreeState()
{
    if (_previouslySelectedItem == null)
        return;

    foreach (RadTreeNode node in radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.Nodes)
    {
        var found = FindNodeByDataBoundItemRecursive(node, _previouslySelectedItem);
        if (found != null)
        {
            radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNode = found;
            found.Expand();
            break;
        }
    }
}

private RadTreeNode? FindNodeByDataBoundItemRecursive(RadTreeNode node, object target)
{
    if (node.DataBoundItem != null && node.DataBoundItem.Equals(target))
        return node;

    foreach (RadTreeNode child in node.Nodes)
    {
        var result = FindNodeByDataBoundItemRecursive(child, target);
        if (result != null)
            return result;
    }

    return null;
}
```

Before reloading or resetting the tree:

### ✅ Fix: Map by `Guid` Instead of Object Reference

Let’s change `nodeStates` from:

to:

```csharp
private Dictionary<Guid, State> nodeStates = new Dictionary<Guid, State>();
```

Then adjust the logic to extract a consistent `Guid` from any node (RateTable, Zone, Rule) during save/restore.

### ✅ Update Save Logic:
```csharp
private void SaveNodeStateRecursive(RadTreeNode node)
{
    var id = GetNodeGuid(node.DataBoundItem);
    if (id != Guid.Empty)
    {
        nodeStates[id] = new State(node.Expanded, node.Selected);
    }

    foreach (RadTreeNode child in node.Nodes)
    {
        SaveNodeStateRecursive(child);
    }
}
```

---

### ✅ Update Restore Logic:
```csharp
private void RestoreNodeStateRecursive(RadTreeNode node)
{
    var id = GetNodeGuid(node.DataBoundItem);
    if (id != Guid.Empty && nodeStates.TryGetValue(id, out var state))
    {
        node.Expanded = state.Expanded;
        node.Selected = state.Selected;
    }

    foreach (RadTreeNode child in node.Nodes)
    {
        RestoreNodeStateRecursive(child);
    }
}
```

```csharp
private Guid GetNodeGuid(object data)
{

        case PricingRuleDto rule: return rule.Id;

}
```

Yeah—good catch. The reason you're seeing `SaveToAPI(rateTable)` fire inside `LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()` is **because of this line:**

```csharp
rateTable.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
```

That means **any time a property on a `RateTableDto` changes, it immediately triggers a save.**

---

### ✅ Why is it saving during load?

Even though `LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()` is **only supposed to fetch and wire data**, it's also:

- Subscribing to `PropertyChanged`
- Subscribing to `CollectionChanged`
- Then calling `SaveToAPI` **during those event subscriptions**

If something mutates data during that setup — like setting up grid data sources or form field bindings — `PropertyChanged` gets triggered. **Boom: auto-save.**

---

### ✅ What to do about it

You probably want to block or defer all saves **until initial setup is done**.

Here's the cleanest fix:

---

### 🔧 Add Guard Flag
```csharp
private bool _isInitializing = false;
```

---

### 🔧 Wrap Load Logic
```csharp
private async Task LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()
{
    _isInitializing = true;

    // ... your current logic ...

    _isInitializing = false;
}
```

---

### 🔧 Update Save Handler Guards
Update your property listeners like this:
```csharp
rateTable.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) =>
{
    if (!_isInitializing)
        await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
};
```

Do the same for:
- `zone.PropertyChanged`
- `rule.PropertyChanged`
- `CollectionChanged`

---

This prevents **any accidental saves triggered by UI bindings or data setup** during load. After initialization is complete, it resumes normal reactive saving.

### ✅ Updated `LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()` with save suppression:
```csharp
private async Task LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()
{
    _isInitializing = true;

    const int maxRetries = 10;
    const int delayMs = 10000;

    for (int i = 1; i <= maxRetries; i++)
    {
        try
        {
            var result = await _tariffViewModel.GetRateTables();
            if (result.Success)
            {
                try
                {
                    if (result.Collection == null)
                    {
                        UpdateStatusStripMessage("Connection Established - Data did not emerge.");
                        SendDektopAlert("API Connection was successful. ERROR: Data not retrieved", "ERROR");
                        return;
                    }

                    _rateTables = result.Collection;
                    InitializeRateTableHashes(_rateTables);

                    foreach (var rateTable in _rateTables)
                    {
                        rateTable.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) =>
                        {
                            if (!_isInitializing)
                                await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                        };

                        rateTable.RateTableZones.CollectionChanged += async (s, e) =>
                        {
                            if (_isInitializing) return;

                            if (e.NewItems != null)
                            {
                                foreach (ZoneDTO zone in e.NewItems)
                                {
                                    zone.PropertyChanged += async (zs, ze) =>
                                    {
                                        if (!_isInitializing)
                                            await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                                    };

                                    foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)
                                    {
                                        rule.PropertyChanged += async (rs, re) =>
                                        {
                                            if (!_isInitializing)
                                                await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                                        };
                                    }
                                }
                            }

                            if (e.OldItems != null)
                            {
                                foreach (ZoneDTO zone in e.OldItems)
                                {
                                    zone.PropertyChanged -= async (zs, ze) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                                    foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)
                                    {
                                        rule.PropertyChanged -= async (rs, re) => await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                                    }
                                }
                            }

                            await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                        };

                        foreach (var zone in rateTable.RateTableZones)
                        {
                            zone.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) =>
                            {
                                if (!_isInitializing)
                                    await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                            };

                            foreach (var rule in zone.ZonePricingRule)
                            {
                                rule.PropertyChanged += async (s, e) =>
                                {
                                    if (!_isInitializing)
                                        await SaveToAPI(rateTable);
                                };
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                catch (Exception ex)
                {
                    UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Connection Failed: {ex.Message}");
                    SendDektopAlert("API Connection failed", "ERROR");
                }

                return;
            }

            UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Attempting to connect to API - Try #{i} ({result.Message ?? "No error detail"})");
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            UpdateStatusStripMessage($"Attempt #{i} failed: {ex.Message}");
        }

        await Task.Delay(delayMs);
    }

    UpdateStatusStripMessage("❌ Failed to connect to API after multiple attempts. Service may be unavailable.");
    SendDektopAlert("Failed to connect to API after multiple attempts. Service may be unavailable.", "ERROR - API Connection Failure");
    _isInitializing = false;
}
```

Yes, absolutely — since `LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()` **reloads the entire structure**, it’s a good idea to **clear and reset relevant data** at the beginning to avoid:

- Duplicated event handlers  
- Memory leaks from retained references  
- Dirty or outdated UI state  
- Hash mismatch confusion due to unchanged reference pointers

---

### ✅ You should **clear** the following at the top of `LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()`:

```csharp
private async Task LoadAPIDataIntoMemory()
{
    _isInitializing = true;

    // 🧹 Clear old bindings/state
    _rateTables?.Clear();
    _rateTables = new List<RateTableDto>();
    _rateTableHashes.Clear();

    // Clear TreeView and UI
    radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.SelectedNodeChanged -= SelectedNodeChanged;
    radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.Nodes.Clear();

    // Optionally reset the current selections
    _currentRateTable = null;
    _currentZone = null;
    _currentPricingRule = null;
```

---

### 🔄 Optionally add at the end before setting `_isInitializing = false`:
```csharp
PopulateTreeView(); // Rebind tree
_isInitializing = false;
```

---

### 🧠 Why this matters:

- **Hashing** will fail silently if the references didn’t change but the data did.
- **Multiple event registrations** lead to multiple `SaveToAPI` calls.
- **Old objects** might still fire `PropertyChanged` if they’re in memory.

        {

            if (e.Node?.DataBoundItem == null) return;



            var data = e.Node.DataBoundItem;



            switch (data)

            {

                case RateTableDto rate:

                



                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != rate.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = rate;

                        _currentPricingRule = null;

                        _currentZone = null;



                    }

                    DatabindTable(_currentRateTable);

                    btnAddRule.Enabled = false;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = true;

                    HideServiceArea(true);

                    HidePricingRules(true);

                    headerLabel.Text = _currentRateTable.TarriffTableName;

                    break;



                case ZoneDTO zone:

                    if (_currentZone == null || _currentZone.Id != zone.Id)

                    {

                        _currentZone = zone;

                        _currentPricingRule = null;

                    }



                    var parentRate = e.Node.Parent?.DataBoundItem as RateTableDto;

                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != parentRate?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = parentRate;

                    }



                    _currentPricingRule = null;

                    DatabindZone(_currentRateTable, _currentZone);

                    btnAddRule.Enabled = true;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = true;

                    HideServiceArea(false);

                    HidePricingRules(true);

                    headerLabel.Text = $"{_currentRateTable?.TarriffTableName} - {_currentZone.ZoneName}";

                    break;



                case PricingRuleDto rule:

                    if (_currentPricingRule == null || _currentPricingRule.Id != rule.Id)

                    {

                        _currentPricingRule = rule;

                    }



                    var newZone = e.Node.Parent?.DataBoundItem as ZoneDTO;

                    if (_currentZone == null || _currentZone.Id != newZone?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentZone = newZone;

                    }



                    var newRateTable = e.Node.Parent?.Parent?.DataBoundItem as RateTableDto;

                    if (_currentRateTable == null || _currentRateTable.Id != newRateTable?.Id)

                    {

                        _currentRateTable = newRateTable;

                    }



                    DataBindPriceRule(_currentRateTable, _currentZone, _currentPricingRule);



                    headerLabel.Text = $"{_currentRateTable?.TarriffTableName} - {_currentZone?.ZoneName} - {_currentPricingRule?.RuleName}";

                    btnAddRule.Enabled = true;

                    btnAddZone.Enabled = false;

                    HidePricingRules(false);

                    HideServiceArea(false);

                    break;

            }

        }



        /// <summary>

        ///

        /// </summary>

        /// <param name="rateTable"></param>

        /// <returns></returns>

        private async Task SaveToAPI(RateTableDto rateTable)

        {

            _pricingRuleBinding.EndEdit();

            _zoneBinding.EndEdit();

            _rateTableBinding.EndEdit();

            radGridWeightCostRatio.EndEdit();

            radGridAccessorials.EndEdit();

            radGrid_ZipCodes.EndEdit();



            var currentHash = GetHash(rateTable);



            if (_rateTableHashes.TryGetValue(rateTable.Id, out var previousHash) && currentHash == previousHash)

                return;



            var result = await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(rateTable);



            if (result.Success && result.returnData is RateTableDto updatedDto)

            {

                rateTable.RowVersion = updatedDto.RowVersion;

                _currentRateTable = updatedDto;

                _rateTableHashes[rateTable.Id] = GetHash(updatedDto); // Update snapshot

            }



            DataBindPriceRule(_currentRateTable, _currentZone, _currentPricingRule);



            return;

        }

        private async Task DeleteNodeAsync(TreeViewNodeModel model)

        {

            switch (model.modelType)

            {

                case "rate":

                    await _tariffViewModel.DeleteRateTable((RateTableDto)model.returnData);



                    break;



                case "zone":

                    var parentRate = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == ((ZoneDTO)model.returnData).RateTableGuid);

                    parentRate?.RateTableZones.Remove((ZoneDTO)model.returnData);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parentRate);

                    break;



                case "rule":

                    var zone = _rateTables.SelectMany(rt => rt.RateTableZones)

                        .FirstOrDefault(z => z.Id == ((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData).ZoneGuid);

                    zone?.ZonePricingRule.Remove((PricingRuleDto)model.returnData);

                    var parent = _rateTables.FirstOrDefault(rt => rt.Id == zone?.RateTableGuid);

                    await _tariffViewModel.UpdateRateTable(parent);

                    break;

            }



            await ReloadUniverseIntoMemory();

            await PopulateTreeView();

        }

        private void SaveNodeStateRecursive(RadTreeNode node)

        {

            var id = GetNodeGuid(node.DataBoundItem);

            if (id != Guid.Empty)

            {

                nodeStates[id] = new State(node.Expanded, node.Selected);

            }



            foreach (RadTreeNode child in node.Nodes)

            {

                SaveNodeStateRecursive(child);

            }

        }





        private void RestoreExpandedStates()

        {

            foreach (RadTreeNode node in radTreeView_TarrifRateTables.Nodes)

        private void RestoreNodeStateRecursive(RadTreeNode node)

        {

            var id = GetNodeGuid(node.DataBoundItem);

            if (id != Guid.Empty && nodeStates.TryGetValue(id, out var state))

            {

                node.Expanded = state.Expanded;

                node.Selected = state.Selected;

            }



            foreach (RadTreeNode child in node.Nodes)

            {

                RestoreNodeStateRecursive(child);

            }

        }
